chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from a number of our companions from Aban ibn Uthman from al-Fadl ibn Abd al-Malik from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who did not have wealth, so some people from his companions performed Hajj on his behalf. I asked: Has he fulfilled the Hajj of Islam? He said: Yes. But when he becomes affluent after that, upon him is that he performs Hajj. I said: And will that Hajj of his be complete or deficient if he did not perform Hajj from his own wealth? He said: Yes. The Hajj of Islam is fulfilled for him, and it will be complete and not deficient. And if he becomes affluent, let him perform Hajj.

He said: And he was asked about a man who has camels, he hires them out and earns from them, so he performs Hajj while he is a renter (of the camels/means). Would that suffice him from his Hajj? Or he carries trade to Mecca, so he performs Hajj and earns wealth in his trade or loses it? Would his Hajj be complete or deficient, or would it not be [complete] until he goes with it to Hajj and does not intend anything else, or he intends both together? Would that fulfill his Hajj? He said: Yes, his Hajj is complete.

key_terms.حَجَّةُ الْإِسْلَامِ: The obligatory Hajj performed once in a lifetime

ai.seo_question: Is a person's Hajj valid if they used borrowed money or hired camels instead of their own wealth?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that Hajj performed using borrowed wealth or hired services is valid and sufficient for the initial obligation (Hajj al-Islam), provided the individual had the means to secure those resources. The Imam further distinguishes this from cases where one merely travels for trade or hires camels without dedicating them specifically for Hajj, confirming that such acts also suffice. This ruling underscores the Shia juristic view that the source of funds (whether owned, borrowed, or hired) does not invalidate the pillar, though financial capacity remains a prerequisite for the obligation to be incumbent.

en.hubeali:
Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Sama’at, from a number of our companions, from Aban Bin usman, from Al Fazl Bin Abdul Malik, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who did not happen to have wealth for him, so he performed Hajj (with the help of) some people from his companions. Has he fulfilled a Hajj of Al-Islam?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes. But when he becomes affluent after that, upon him would be that he performs Hajj (again)’. I said, ‘And would that Hajj of his be complete or deficient when he did not perform Hajj from his own wealth?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes. The Hajj of Al-Islam has been fulfilled from it, and would happen to be complete, and would not be with deficiency; and if he becomes affluent, so let him perform Hajj (again)’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘And he<sup>asws</sup> was asked about the man who happened to have the camel for him which he has hired. So rides and performs Hajj upon it, and he has hired it. Would it suffice him from his Hajj; or he carries the merchandise to Makkah (for trade), so he performs Hajj, and he earns the wealth in his trading or loses, would his Hajj happen to be complete or deficient, or it would not happen to be until he goes with it to the Hajj not intending something else (e.g. trade), or he intends both of these together, would that fulfill his Hajj?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, his Hajj is complete’.
en.sarwar: 2. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from ibn Sama‘ah from A number of our people have narrated from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from al-Fadl ibn ‘Abd al-Malik who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who does not have any assets but people helped him to perform al-Hajj; if it is sufficient for Hajjahta al-Islam. He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, but if later he becomes affluent, he is required to perform al-Hajj again.’ I then asked, ‘The kind of al-Hajj that he has performed, is it complete or defective because he has not performed it from his own assets?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, it is sufficient for Hajjahta al-Islam and it will be complete, not defective; however, if he becomes affluent he must perform al-Hajj again.’

He (the Imam) was asked about a man who has camel for hire who finds a passenger and performs al-Hajj while he is hired; is his al-Hajj sufficient Hajjah for him; also if he carries assets for trade to Makkah, then he finds a certain amount of assets from his trade or suffers losses. Is his al-Hajj complete or defective or it is not al-Hajj, unless he goes to Makkah just for al-Hajj without any intention for other things or that he has intention for al-Hajj as well as other matters? Is this kind of al-Hajj sufficient for his al-Hajj? He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, his al-Hajj is complete.’”
